\[
\Omega = \{ x : m(x) > 0 \},
\qquad
\Delta^2 I = 0 \text{ in } \Omega,\quad I = I_0 \text{ outside } \Omega
\quad \text{(biharmonic)}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(m\): The selection, from 0 to 1
- \(\Omega\): The hole
- \(I_0\): The image
- \(\Delta\): The Laplacian, the sum of the second derivatives

The hole Omega is every pixel the selection m touches. Pixels outside it never change. All three methods make the fill meet the image smoothly at the edge of the hole. Biharmonic inpainting asks for the smoothest surface that meets the image with its slope, so it solves the biharmonic equation in the hole. Telea's method fills the hole from its edge inward, in order of distance, as found by fast marching. Each new pixel is a weighted mean of the known pixels within the radius, each moved on by its gradient. The Navier-Stokes method of Bertalmio, Bertozzi and Sapiro carries the smoothness Delta I into the hole along the lines of equal brightness, as a 2D fluid carries its vorticity. So edges that meet the hole continue into it. The Inspector shows the equations of the chosen method.
